title: Stem Cells: The Body's Blank Slates
hook: Some cells haven't decided what to be yet — they can become muscle, nerve, or blood, and that flexibility makes them a frontier of medicine.
key_points: Stem cells are unspecialized cells that can divide and become other cell types.
They self-renew, making more stem cells, and differentiate into specialized cells.
Embryonic stem cells can become almost any cell type; adult stem cells are more limited.
Researchers hope to use them to repair tissue and treat disease.
content_html: Most cells in your body have a fixed job — a skin cell stays a skin cell. Stem cells are the exception: they're unspecialized, meaning they haven't committed to a role yet. That blank-slate quality, plus their ability to keep dividing, makes them central to how the body builds and repairs itself, and a major focus of medical research.
extra_html: Stem cells are defined by two abilities: they can self-renew, dividing to produce more stem cells, and they can differentiate, maturing into specialized types such as blood, muscle, or nerve cells. As NIH's MedlinePlus explains, embryonic stem cells are the most versatile, able to become almost any cell type, while adult (or tissue) stem cells are more restricted, usually repairing the tissue they live in. Scientists are working to harness this potential to grow replacement tissue and treat conditions like spinal cord injury and diabetes — though embryonic stem cell research also raises ethical questions about where those cells come from.

related.title: Mitosis: One Cell Becomes Two
related.hook: Right now, millions of your cells are copying their DNA and splitting in two — the everyday process that lets you grow, heal, and replace worn-out cells.

related.title: The Cell's Tiny Organs
related.hook: Inside a single cell sits a whole working city — a control room, power plants, factories, and shipping lanes, each a structure called an organelle.

flashcards.prompt: What makes a stem cell different from most other cells?
flashcards.back_html: A stem cell is unspecialized — it hasn't committed to one job. It can both make copies of itself and develop into specialized cells like muscle or nerve.

flashcards.prompt: What are the two defining abilities of a stem cell?

choices.text: Self-renewal and differentiation into other cell types

flashcards.explanation_html: Stem cells can self-renew (make more stem cells) and differentiate (mature into specialized cell types) — the combination is what defines them.

flashcards.prompt: How do embryonic stem cells generally compare to adult stem cells?

choices.text: Embryonic ones can become a wider range of cell types
Adult ones can become any cell type, embryonic ones cannot
They are identical in every way

flashcards.explanation_html: Embryonic stem cells can develop into nearly any cell type, while adult stem cells are usually limited to the tissues they came from.
